text:
alex_t: FYI - ~2k targets for svc/edge-ingress in eu-west-1 were marked Unhealthy ~5m ago, ALB started deregistering.
deploy-bot: Deployment egress-ip-allocator v2 rolled out to cluster-prod-eu at 2364829000
maria_ops: did we have any recent network changes? @oncall-jess
oncall-jess: I'm looking. Any obvious 5xx from the app?
alex_t: curl from inside node -> pod shows 200 on /health. ALB healthcheck from LB->10.10.0.0/24 returns 504 or TCP reset.
alex_t: paste:
```
$ curl -v http://10.10.3.45:8080/health
* Connected to 10.10.3.45 (10.10.3.45) port 8080 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.10.3.45
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
```
But from ALB nodes we see:
```
ALB -> 10.10.3.45:8080, tcp reset / timeout
```
saml: Could be SNAT port exhaustion or source IP change; ALB healthchecks come from a set of node IPs, if egress IP rotated they might be hitting unexpected iptables rules.
maria_ops: run `kubectl get endpoints svc/edge-ingress -n edge -o wide` and `kubectl describe node <node>` to see kube-proxy restart
oncall-jess: I see kube-proxy rolled on nodes 3/4/5 ~2364829050 due to flannel upgrade
saml: That would reassign ephemeral source ports and potentially break established NAT mappings for ALB healthcheck flows.
alex_t: Also noticed we recently enabled the new "egress-ip-affinity" option in the allocator config this morning. Could be allocator rotating egress IP assignments during the rollout.
maria_ops: Check conntrack counters: `sudo conntrack -S | grep -E \"tcp|established\"` and SNAT table entries
alex_t: Ran conntrack dump — seeing many TIME_WAIT and some entries with reuse warnings. SNAT ports per node reported ~62k in use on one node (out of ~64k).
oncall-jess: I temporarily rolled back egress-ip-allocator to v1 at 2364829120
deploy-bot: Rollback triggered: egress-ip-allocator -> v1 by oncall-jess (change: revert affinity config)
maria_ops: Waiting for LB to re-evaluate. Can someone force target re-register with aws cli or just wait for healthchecks?
saml: ALB will recheck health every 10s; once healthchecks succeed it will register. If SNAT was causing TCP resets, rollback should clear it.
alex_t: Confirmed: targets started transitioning to healthy at 2364829185, registrations coming back in waves.
maria_ops: Preliminary root cause: egress-ip-affinity rotation + kube-proxy flurry -> SNAT port collisions/timeouts -> ALB healthchecks suffered TCP resets and timed out. Follow-up: allocator should avoid rotating egress IPs for nodes with active LB healthchecks and we need a conntrack saturation alert.
oncall-jess: filing ticket RINF-2312 and adding alert: node_conntrack_usage > 90% -> page oncall.
alex_t: thanks all :thumbsup:
